title: Update on Recognition and Verification of Health Passports
what_it_is: Update on Recognition and Verification of Health Passports

sections.label: ITP and vaccination certificate recognition
sections.summary: Since 1 May 2021 travellers to Singapore can use the ITP to share pre-departure PCR test results, and Singapore is in bilateral talks with Australia, Malaysia and Republic of Korea on mutual recognition of vaccination certificates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Since 1 May 2021, passengers travelling to Singapore have been able to use the ITP to share their pre-departure Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) test results when checking-in with their airlines, as well as on-arrival at the immigration checkpoints at Changi Airport.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Singapore is also in bilateral discussions with several countries on establishing mechanisms for the mutual recognition of vaccination certificates, including with Australia, Malaysia and Republic of Korea.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: We have set up inter-agency bilateral working groups with these countries and are exchanging information on how we may mutually verify the authenticity of each other’s certificates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: This includes the exchange of public keys for the verification of digital certificates and the exchange of specimen copies for the verification of physical certificates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: These discussions will likely take some time, as countries and regions are at different stages of progress in vaccinating their respective populations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, these multilateral and regional discussions are useful in laying the groundwork for us to re-open travel for vaccinated individuals between Singapore and these countries when we are ready to do so.

sections.label: Verifying vaccination done properly
sections.summary: The passage asks how to verify that residents of different countries are vaccinated properly, and says the ITP and other certificates should be viewed as a two-step process.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Two, how are we going to verify that this vaccination that each of the residents in the different country get are in the appropriate manner, that they are vaccinated properly?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I think we should view the ITP and also other forms of such certificates, as a two-step process.

sections.label: Restrictions not automatically lifted
sections.summary: The passage states that coming from a particular country and testing negative or being vaccinated does not automatically do away with some restrictions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Just because the individual comes from a particular country and has been tested negative or has been vaccinated, does not mean that we automatically do away with some of the restrictions.
